name: Year 12
note: Year 12 is the first year of most A level courses.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Differentiating powers of x
lessons.summary: Find the gradient of a curve by differentiating.
lessons.curriculum: A level mathematics: differentiate x to a power, with constant multiples, sums and differences, and find gradients
pages: Differentiation finds the gradient of a curve at any point. The result is called the derivative, written dy/dx.
To differentiate x to a power, multiply by the power and then take 1 from the power. So if y = x³, then dy/dx = 3x².
Differentiate each term on its own. A constant on its own becomes 0. If y = 4x² + 3x + 7, then dy/dx = 8x + 3.
To find the gradient at a point, put in its x value. At x = 2, the gradient of y = 4x² + 3x + 7 is 8 × 2 + 3 = 19.

check.question: What is dy/dx if y = 5x²?
check.explanation: Multiply by the power, 2, and take 1 from the power: 5 × 2x = 10x.

lessons.subject: Biology
lessons.title: The structure of DNA
lessons.summary: Learn how DNA is built from nucleotides and held together by base pairs.
lessons.curriculum: A level biology: the structure of DNA, including nucleotides and complementary base pairing
pages: DNA is a polymer made of monomers called nucleotides. Each nucleotide has a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar and a nitrogenous base.
There are 4 bases in DNA: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C) and guanine (G).
DNA has 2 strands that twist into a double helix. Hydrogen bonds between complementary bases hold the strands together: A pairs with T, and C pairs with G.
A and T form 2 hydrogen bonds, and C and G form 3. Base pairing lets DNA copy itself accurately by semi-conservative replication.

check.question: Which base pairs with cytosine in DNA?
check.explanation: Cytosine pairs with guanine, joined by 3 hydrogen bonds.

lessons.subject: Chemistry
lessons.title: Amount of substance: the mole
lessons.summary: Use moles to count particles and work out masses.
lessons.curriculum: A level chemistry: amount of substance, the mole and the Avogadro constant
pages: Chemists count particles in moles. One mole of a substance contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles. This number is the Avogadro constant.
Relative formula mass (Mr) is the sum of the relative atomic masses in a formula. For water, H2O, Mr = 1 + 1 + 16 = 18.
Amount in moles = mass ÷ Mr. So 36 grams (g) of water is 36 ÷ 18 = 2 moles.

check.question: How many moles are in 88g of carbon dioxide, which has an Mr of 44?

lessons.subject: Economics
lessons.title: Supply and demand
lessons.summary: See how buyers and sellers set the price in a market.
lessons.curriculum: A level economics: price determination, and how supply and demand interact in markets
pages: Demand is how much of a good people want to buy at each price. When the price falls, demand usually rises.
Supply is how much producers want to sell at each price. When the price rises, supply usually rises too.
The market settles where demand equals supply. This is called the equilibrium price.
If demand rises and supply stays the same, the equilibrium price rises. This is why tickets for popular concerts can cost a lot.

check.question: Demand for a product rises but supply does not change. What happens to the equilibrium price?
check.explanation: More buyers compete for the same supply, so the price rises.
